summary: POC scoping call to size reserved GPU capacity and autoscale/burst strategy. CloudFlux wants deterministic latency under 300ms p95 for chat workloads, cost target under $0.005/token, 4-6 week POC with benchmarks comparing Redwood Dedicated and their current self-hosted infra.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE); Priya Rao (CloudFlux Head of ML); Ethan Park (CloudFlux Infra); Salma Idris (CloudFlux CTO)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick us off. today goal is to scope the poc for capacity and autoscale — reserved gpus, burst strategy and fallback policies. want to confirm success criteria and the timeline.
[00:12] Priya Rao: yep thanks, maya. quick context: we run a chat assistant, avg 180 tokens per response, peaks obviously higher. currently self-hosted on a mix of G4/H100-ish infra, but ops overhead is high. main metrics: p95 latency under 300ms, and keep cost per token under roughly 0.005. POC needs to prove we can hit those.
[00:28] Liam Ortiz: got it. maya and i will go through our recommended sizes and how autoscale/burst works on Redwood Dedicated, also fallback to cheaper variants.
[00:35] Ethan Park: for concurrency, our q2 spike load is around 120 concurrent chat sessions; sustained concurrent about 40-60. we can provide traces.
[00:44] Salma Idris: timeline: we want a decision within 6 weeks if the POC shows production parity. so POC ideally 4 weeks of benchmarking plus a week for eval and legal.

[05:00] Liam Ortiz: ok, on capacity — for 180 tokens average and your concurrency numbers, initial recommendation is to reserve 4 GPUs (H100 if you prioritize latency), with burst pool of 2 additional preemptible GPUs to cover spikes. that gives room for autoscale to allocate more when KV cache misses happen or longer contexts.
[05:22] Priya Rao: question — how does bursting interact with billing? are we billed for burst only when used?
[05:30] Maya Chen: yes. reserved capacity billed as monthly commit for the poc term but burst is pay-as-you-go. we can also structure a short-term reserved seat for the POC (monthly pro-rate) + credits for burst.
[06:05] Ethan Park: ok, what's a realistic throughput per GPU we should expect? we currently get about 25 qps per h100 for 512 token contexts on our stack, but that might be different for your runtime.
[06:18] Liam Ortiz: great callout — our kernel selection and continuous batching can push that up. for a 180-token median, expect roughly 40-60 concurrent streams per H100-equivalent for interactive latency SLOs. p95 depends on tail and cold-starts. with prefix/KV cache warm, we generally see stable p95s under 250-300ms on H100. on A100 you'll see slightly higher latency but lower cost.

[10:00] Priya Rao: talk me through fallback policies — if reserved is saturated and burst exhausted, we can't have large user-facing errors.
[10:10] Liam Ortiz: two recommended fallback layers: 1) model variant fallback — shorter or quantized variant (e.g., 8-bit quantized smaller model) with graceful degradation; 2) region/fallback routing to less-busy pools or lower-tier instances with a slightly higher latency but still usable. you can customize per-route.
[10:35] Maya Chen: and we support automatic canary+rollback for any model changes, so if quality falls we can switch back. we also keep detailed token-level tracing so you can audit decisions.

[15:00] Ethan Park: i want to make sure we can reproduce benchmarks locally. what tooling/metrics will you expose?
[15:07] Liam Ortiz: during the POC we provide a benchmark harness — a set of artifacts: load scripts, synthetic traces generator, and dashboards. core metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, qps, GPU utilization, cost per token. we'll need your representative traces and a golden prompt set for qualitative checks.
[15:28] Priya Rao: we'll share traces; note that our dataset has higher tail length — 10% of requests are 1k+ tokens. how should we account in sizing?
[15:40] Liam Ortiz: plan for tail capacity — either reserve an extra GPU or configure burst policy to prioritize tail requests while throttling less-critical background calls. also use prefix caching to reduce compute for repeated prompts.

[20:00] Salma Idris: security questions — we need to ensure keys use our KMS, audit logs, and VPC peering for the POC.
[20:10] Maya Chen: yes we support customer-managed KMS and VPC peering for Redwood Private or Dedicated with private control plane. we'll include SOC2/ISO docs and the integration notes in the security pack.

[25:00] Priya Rao: success criteria — let me list and confirm: 1) p95 latency <= 300ms for 95% of regular traffic (not including extreme 1k+ tails) 2) peak stability for 2x current spikes without errors 3) cost target within 15% of 0.005/token 4) audit and KMS integration validated.
[25:18] Maya Chen: that's clear. we propose a measurement period of at least one full week of representative traffic during POC to validate.

[30:00] Ethan Park: for the reserved GPU mix — you're suggesting H100s; what about A100 to reduce cost? tradeoffs?
[30:10] Liam Ortiz: A100 is a good cost balance — lower p95 but cheaper. H100 gives best latency headroom for tail-heavy workloads. for the POC we can do mixed pool: 2x H100 reserved + 2x A100 reserved + 2x burst H100. this allows us to route latency-critical requests to H100s and other requests to A100.
[30:40] Priya Rao: can the routing be real-time? like per-request decisioning?
[30:48] Liam Ortiz: yes, smart routing can be per-policy — route by latency sensitivity, user tier, or cost. automatic fallback when a pool reaches target utilization.

[35:00] Maya Chen: on timelines — recommended POC flow: week 0: kickoff + infra setup (VPC peering, KMS), week 1: smoke tests and baseline benchmarking, week 2-3: stress tests and tuning, week 4: validation and review with stakeholders. legal and billing usually parallel. overall 4-6 weeks.
[35:20] Salma Idris: legal needs a short SOW and data handling addendum. we'll have our counsel loop in once pricing is shared.

[40:00] Priya Rao: for benchmarks, will you run head-to-head against our current infra or just Redwood?
[40:08] Liam Ortiz: ideally both — we can ingest your traces and replay them against Redwood Dedicated and, if you provide endpoint access or logs, against your stack so we can present apples-to-apples. note: differences in tokenization or model variants can affect numbers, we'll call those out.

[45:00] Ethan Park: question: what's the cold-start behavior for new model versions and how does cache warm-up work?
[45:10] Liam Ortiz: cold-starts incur kv-cache misses and longer latency. we recommend warmup scripts during deploys; for POC we can pre-warm based on your golden prompts. continuous batching also reduces variance.

[50:00] Priya Rao: financial — we need an estimate for reserved GPU monthly pro-rate for the POC: can you ballpark?
[50:08] Maya Chen: rough ballpark: H100 reserved equivalent for POC rate around $12k/month per GPU (this is a placeholder, we'll send exact POC pricing). A100 around $6k-$8k/month. burst usage is billed on usage. for a 4-week POC we'll pro-rate and can include credits.
[50:34] Priya Rao: that initial number helps. we'll evaluate against total TCO including ops.

[55:00] Maya Chen: recap / next steps: 1) liam will produce a capacity plan with recommended GPU mix and autoscale config, 2) maya will send POC pricing and contract template, 3) cloudflux to share traces and golden prompts, 4) security pack delivered. we'll aim to have pricing and security docs by 2026-05-22.
[55:18] Priya Rao: correct. and we'll confirm VPC peering details and test dataset by 2026-05-25.
[55:30] Salma Idris: thanks everyone — this aligns with our internal timeline.
[55:35] Maya Chen: great, thank you all. we'll follow up via email and schedule the benchmark window.
[59:50] (call ends)
